risks.description: In-flight workflow state held in the durable store is lost or corrupted when the process/callback service restarts, so the workflow cannot resume.
risks.basis: AC 'workflow state survives a process restart' (weight 3), still PENDING; diff moves state out of in-process cache.

risks.description: A write that fails partway leaves a partially applied workflow row (dangling reference / half-updated state) instead of atomically rolling back.
risks.basis: AC 'a failed write leaves no partially applied workflow' (weight 3), PENDING.

risks.description: Rebuilding workflow state from history re-executes an already-performed external effect, causing a duplicate business action.
risks.basis: AC 'rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect' (weight 3), PENDING.

risks.description: A read issued after a committed write returns stale state (e.g. from a residual in-process cache), so callers act on an outdated view.
risks.basis: AC 'a read after a write never returns stale state' (weight 2), PENDING.

risks.description: The durable workflow store table is never actually created in the canonical schema, so state silently remains process-local and cannot survive restart.
risks.basis: Unit U-P5-1 requires state moved to the durable workflow store; if the schema lacks the table the move is incomplete.

scenarios.title: Workflow store survives a live callback restart intact
scenarios.purpose: Restart the callback service and confirm the durable workflow SQLite store is still structurally intact (not corrupted/truncated) afterward, exercising the real restart path rather than a simulated one.
scenarios.rationale: The whole unit exists so state outlives a process restart; a live restart of the only restartable service is the most direct probe of that promise.
scenarios.generating_risk: A restart loses or corrupts the durable workflow state so the workflow cannot resume (R1).
scenarios.requirement_reference: workflow state survives a process restart
scenarios.isolation_note: Only restarts the callback service and runs a read-only PRAGMA integrity_check; it does not insert, update, or delete any workflow rows, so it cannot contaminate later scenarios.

scenarios.title: Fault-injection checkpoint matrix leaves no partial workflow
scenarios.purpose: Run the phase3 checkpoint matrix, which exercises write/checkpoint combinations under injected faults, to confirm a failed write never commits a partially applied workflow.
scenarios.rationale: The matrix suite is the only approved lever that injects mid-write failures across states; it directly targets the atomicity acceptance criterion.
scenarios.generating_risk: A write failing partway leaves a half-applied workflow row instead of rolling back atomically (R2).
scenarios.requirement_reference: a failed write leaves no partially applied workflow
scenarios.isolation_note: Assumed to run against its own temporary databases (pytest fixtures), not the driver_probe live store; read-only with respect to shared state.

scenarios.title: Rebuild from history does not re-execute effects and reads are not stale
scenarios.purpose: Run the witness and claim-CAS suites together (the single approved invocation) to confirm rebuilding state from history does not re-fire an effect and that compare-and-swap writes prevent stale reads.
scenarios.rationale: Witness tests guard effect-replay and CAS tests guard read-after-write freshness; both are the recovery invariants the durable-store move must preserve.
scenarios.generating_risk: Rebuilding state from history re-executes an already-performed external effect, and/or a post-write read returns stale state (R3, R4).
scenarios.requirement_reference: rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect
scenarios.isolation_note: Assumed to use pytest-managed temporary stores, not the driver_probe live database; does not mutate shared state.

scenarios.title: Durable workflow store table exists in the canonical schema
scenarios.purpose: Build the canonical schema in isolation and confirm a workflow-related table is created, verifying the state actually moved into the durable schema rather than remaining process-local.
scenarios.rationale: Restart survival is impossible if the durable schema has no workflow table; this checks the precondition that the store was truly relocated.
scenarios.generating_risk: The durable workflow table is never created in the canonical schema, so state stays in-process and cannot survive restart (R5).
scenarios.requirement_reference: workflow state survives a process restart
scenarios.isolation_note: The probe writes only into a fresh tempfile.mkdtemp() directory it creates itself; it never touches shared or live state.

actions.name: schema-probe
actions.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sqlite3,tempfile,os,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from freight_recon.schema import create_canonical_schema; p=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),'probe.sqlite3'); c=sqlite3.connect(p); create_canonical_schema(c); print(sorted(r[0] for r in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")))"

scenarios.title: Full canonical suite passes after the store migration
scenarios.purpose: Run the full canonical test suite as a regression guard to confirm moving workflow state to the durable store did not break existing behavior across the unit.
scenarios.rationale: A store relocation touches read/write paths broadly; a full-suite pass is the cheapest signal that no adjacent behavior regressed.
scenarios.generating_risk: The migration silently breaks an existing workflow path not covered by the targeted matrices.
scenarios.isolation_note: Runs the pytest suite against its own fixtures/temp stores; does not mutate the driver_probe live database.

assumptions: The phase3 suites (checkpoint_matrix, witness, claim_cas) are the components encoding the durable-store invariants — restart/checkpoint atomicity, effect-replay avoidance, and compare-and-swap read freshness — because those are the only approved fault-injection levers available.
'callback' is the service whose restart meaningfully exercises the process-restart recovery path for workflow state.

The targeted pytest invocations run against pytest-managed temporary databases rather than data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3, so they do not contaminate the live store checked in S1.
The durable workflow store table is part of create_canonical_schema and its name contains the substring 'workflow'.
unresolved_questions: The exact table and column names of data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 were not provided, so I could not author precise SQL invariant queries (e.g. duplicate-effect detection via GROUP BY ... HAVING count(*)>1, or dangling-reference detection for partial writes) directly against the live store; those invariants are exercised only through the pytest matrices.

No approved command seeds a workflow, commits a write, or forces a mid-write crash against the running app at http://127.0.0.1:8001, so live read-after-write staleness (weight 2) and live atomicity/idempotency cannot be observed end-to-end and are covered only via the test suites — the stale-read AC in particular has no dedicated live probe.

Whether the driver_probe workflow.sqlite3 contains seeded workflow rows is unknown, so S1 can only assert the store is structurally intact after restart (PRAGMA integrity_check ok), not that specific pre-restart data survived.
If the durable workflow table name does not contain the substring 'workflow', S4's expectation is wrong against a correct product — the actual table name should be confirmed.
